terra.problem: The joke compares longing to lunging at a cooling rack. The actions do not match, and the writer does not say he lunges.
Saying the writer's days feel long adds an unmarked guess about his feelings.
The writer's question does not establish that he has not yet arrived. The explanation turns the question into a conclusion about where he is.
The text does not place the writer in a room or describe him walking to God's presence.
The text does not say the writer was not weeping during the procession.
The verse says he remembers God, not that he starts remembering Him at that point.
Saying the writer is underwater turns the poetic image of waves rolling over him into a literal event.
The verse does not say whether anyone is sleeping.
The writer says he will go to the altar; the text does not say he is already there when he speaks.
The text does not say what anyone else at the altar is doing, or that the writer is bringing a harp there.
“Wrong psalm” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
